output.technical_predicate: Withdrawal of an optional consent (here: the "insights" purpose that generates repayment reports) must be as easy as giving it, must be preceded by information, and must stop future report generation — including already queued report jobs and any retries — while leaving an unaffected subscriber's queued report deliverable.
applicability_facts: Scenario: two borrowers opt in (insights consent) and queue reports; one withdraws before execution; the queue is reopened and drained twice; the other borrower remains eligible.

store.py:0092-0098 preference() accepts purpose 'insights' with value 'off' and, on that transition, cancels queued 'report' jobs for that owner's cases (UPDATE jobs SET state='cancelled' WHERE kind='report' AND state='queued' AND cid IN (SELECT id FROM cases WHERE owner=?)).
store.py:0137-0139 drain() only executes a 'report' job when enabled(db, owner, 'insights') is true, so a withdrawn consent blocks execution even if a report job were still queued.
store.py:0126 drain() selects only state='queued' jobs, so cancelled jobs are not re-executed on a second drain (no retry path).
views.py:0033-0036 renders the privacy choices with a 'Switch off' control for an enabled purpose, i.e. withdrawal is offered through the same form/route as opt-in.
store.py:0009 NOTICE and views.py:0024-0025, 0033 state beforehand that insights are optional and can be switched off at any time as easily as on, and that withdrawal applies to future processing.
store.py:0098 cancellation is scoped by owner, so the other borrower's queued report job is untouched and remains eligible.
relevant_exceptions: No exception applies: the scenario stipulates an adult, EU-established private controller and a voluntary optional consent, so no Art. 7(3) exemption or legal-retention override is in play.
The 'objection' purpose (store.py:0096-0098) is a separate direct-marketing control and is not the withdrawal mechanism for the insights consent; it is not relied on here.
required_controls: Symmetric withdrawal control: the same /preference form and route used to switch insights on also switches it off (views.py:0033-0036; app.py:0085-0087).
Prior information: NOTICE text and the privacy-choices copy disclose optionality, ease of withdrawal and future-only effect (store.py:0009; views.py:0024-0025, 0033).
Cancellation of already queued work: preference(...,'insights','off') sets queued 'report' jobs to 'cancelled' for that owner's cases (store.py:0096-0098).
Execution-time gate: drain() refuses to produce a report unless insights consent is currently enabled (store.py:0137).
No retry of cancelled work: drain() only processes state='queued' jobs, so repeated drains do not resurrect cancelled reports (store.py:0126, 0143).
Owner-scoped effect: cancellation and the enabled() check are per owner, preserving the unaffected borrower's queued report (store.py:0088-0090, 0098, 0137).
assessment_limits: Assessment is static reading of the supplied source only; no code was executed, no database was opened, and no drain was run.
The scenario's 'queue reopened and drained twice' outcome is taken as stipulated; the source shows the mechanisms (cancellation, enabled() gate, queued-only selection) but not runtime results.
Only the insights/report withdrawal path is assessed; promotions, objection, and other Art. 7/17/18 controls are out of scope for this rule.
No claim is made about upstream or hidden implementation beyond the three supplied files.
No legal deadline or additional obligation is inferred beyond the stated Art. 7(3) technical predicate.
